reading:
Flight Console's language has always been liked, and what sank each version was costume or a code the family had to learn. In the main rounds it lost on tracked mono caps, 23 small targets, zero-padding, FIG captions, CONSOLE nn / HOLDS / T-minus, an annunciator that repeated the Status lists, and a chat with only one side. In tour round 1 the costume came off and two children tied from opposite ends of the panel.

Lamps and Ladders (graft, 7.53, carried) won feedback, soul and style (8.3 / 8.0 / 8.0) with instruments that carry real light:
- the moving-coil spend meter ("the best single artefact in the heat", "the best single instrument");
- jewelled pilot lamps, and the lit live leg of the flight plan from Now to Next;
- lit tubes in thin cases.

Flight Console, Go (refine, 7.51, not carried) won interaction 8, type 7.5, usability 7.5 and skeptic 7.5 with plain state language:
- leg lengths written over the arcs, and stops numbered to the rows;
- WORKING/OFF in words inside dark annunciator windows;
- two-line due dates (words in sans over the date in mono);
- one-click Show keys and an Edit key on every row;
- a 3px amber edge on late rows;
- "What's the plan?" printed inside the box's frame ("the best placement").

What sank Lamps and Ladders in the lower lenses:
- The per-hop ladders read as signal or battery bars, a code repeating "in 4 days" (four lenses; the device is now retired).
- The amber setup ladder read as hazard striping.
- Zero-padding (05, 02) is costume to every lens.
- On To do, a lamp column sits beside the checkbox and reads as a second control. The Add action has no visible green primary.
- Status has about 250px of empty slate above its first row, and boxed lamp cells where ruled rows would do.
- Six rail links come before the box in Tab order, and counts are said twice (the rail's Late 2 beside the head's "2 late").
- The chat wire stops after two stops.
- The title "Tell Vera what's next." was the weakest new title in all eight notes. It narrows the job and doubles the NEXT UP legend.
- The skeptic called it almost a duplicate of Go on Home, Plans and To do.

Also held against the lineage: the Plans month track is 80% past; the Next up tube floats small; the greeting pool is weak; the AVG pointer sits on top of $0; restaurant swatches are in amber (amber leaking into a kind); cards have a dotted "punched" top edge that reads as texture noise.

To win, the lineage needs:
- One merged system with a single lamp code and no second code. Keep the instruments and the phosphor on a short list: the meter, the jewels, the live leg, curved-glass tubes at full strength, the lit key word, and at most two lit readout windows.
- Every count said once, in plain tabular figures.
- Content changes where the page is weakest: Plans' dead past, Status's head, To do's two left-edge marks, setup's length.
- Coming up and the rows joined by numbered stops.
- The chat hung on its own line from Vera's mark down to the box.
- "What's the plan?" set inside the box.

The lessons say a refine that only cleans looks like its parent at thumbnail size. So the refinement must merge Go's clarity into Lamps and Ladders' light. The graft must replace weak parts rather than add devices beside them, and must draw data the page already holds.

briefs.name: Lamps and Legs
briefs.title: What’s the *plan*? It keeps the best title the lineage has found (Go's, and the tour's most-favoured, first or joint first in 13 of 16 notes). 'plan' names the whole job: weekends, outings, the calendar, reminders. It is the family's own kitchen-table phrase, an invitation to tell Vera something, and 16 characters, so it holds one line on a phone at 32px. It drops 'next', which doubled the NEXT UP legend on the tube beside it and left out ideas and wishes. It is set inside the box's frame, which usability called the best placement in the heat, in Plex Sans Condensed 600 at 36px with a true curly apostrophe. Only 'plan' is lit (.glow, the kit's E1 two-layer halo), and nothing else on Home glows with the word 'plan'.
briefs.hypothesis: The lineage's two round-1 designs tied (7.53 and 7.51) from opposite lenses. Lamps and Ladders' instruments took feedback, soul and style; Go's plain state language took interaction, type, usability and skeptic. Merge them: keep every lit instrument (meter, jewels, live leg, tubes) and put Go's words and numbering where Lamps and Ladders used codes (leg lengths, WORKING/OFF, two-line dates, Edit keys, the title in the frame). Remove every code the family had to learn: ladders, zero-padding, the To do lamp column, the setup hazard ladder. Then no lens has a standing fault left, and the parent's 8.0 lenses are no longer pulled down by 6.5 to 7.0 ones. Adding Aglow's curved glass, a tall Next up tube and a full greeting pool answers soul's and the skeptic's 'phosphor under-returned'. The aim is a mean near 8, level with Lit Manual.
briefs.brief: Start from t1-console-graft's palette, sheet.css and templates. Keep its idea, its three materials (slate console / flight-plan line / phosphor light), its bays under one 2px top rule, its lamp code (jewel = on, steel dot = waiting, pewter ring = off, amber bar = needs a look, red ring = stopped, always with words) and its type scale (44 title / 36 question / 22 head / 16 text / 14 small / 13 label, 24 rail figure; Plex Sans, Plex Sans Condensed heads, Plex Mono only for figures and times, VT323 only on glass). GLOBAL 1. Figures: remove every '%02d' format (home.html rail cells, status.html, tasks.html, plans_month.html, settings.html) and write 5, 2, 12. Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every figure. Use text-wrap: balance on heads and pretty on paragraphs. 2. Ladders out: delete the ladder() and nearness() macros in _ui.html and the .ladder rules ('The lamp ladder' section). That also takes out the chin ladder in the Next up case (.crt-chin .ladder), the hop ladders and the setup gutter ladder. The chin keeps its groove and the power jewel. 3. Flight-plan ink: --ditto #a191bd becomes a low-chroma period steel-cyan, #8fbfdc (about h225, kept off teal). --ditto-2 becomes #56707e for flown legs. Lines stay 1.5px; stop rings take the same colour and their numbers are in ink. 4. Colour: amber keeps one job. The restaurant swatch and the 'Something to eat' icon go to clay: set the people token to #bf8a6a, and move seasons to #d9795f if the colour-distance check warns against it. Amber #e3a651 then means only late or needs a look. 5. The readout rail (rail() macro, '.rail' in 'The readout rail'): - It runs the full width of its bay in equal cells. - Each cell is one 56px row: the label (13px, 600, sentence case) at the left, a dotted leader, and the figure (Plex Mono, 24px, tabular) right-aligned at the cell's end. The whole cell is a link, 44px or more. - Only two cells may give off light: Today, as the console clock (the date in a small sunk green-black glass window in phosphor, with the E1 halo and 1-in-3 scanlines), and Late when above 0 (the same window in amber phosphor, glow built from --amber). Every other figure is matte ink. 6. Phosphor, on the short list only: - The mark and its cursor (E2); one lit primary per view (E3); fields while typed in (E4); focus (E5); the top haze (E6). - Home's pool (E7) at full strength: the pixel 1px under Send should read about (37,80,52), with scanlines only inside the pool. - The tubes (E12-E15) with Aglow's curved glass: t1-b/variants/t1-console-mut/sheet.css lines 1404-1430 ('The tubes: real curved glass': border-radius 22px/27px, the gasket ring, the corner-weighted falloff, the second reflection low right). - The radar at full persistence, with Aglow's blip sizes (same file, around line 1480); her glyph screen (E19); the jewels (E20); the live leg; the meter's needle. - Make the Next up power-on (E16) visible in the motion-on frames: the content opens from a line, from opacity .05 at 0ms to open by about 450ms (animation 0.7s, delay .05s). - Everything else is matte. HOME 1. The welcome console (.welcome.console) keeps its DOM order: speaker line, box, ways to start, then the Next up tube. - The question sits inside the box's frame (templates/_ask.html h1.ask-question, keeping the
briefs.borrows:
The judges' fixes, most-cited first, with the lenses that asked:
1. Drop the zero-padding everywhere. Asked by every lens across the two designs: feedback, soul, style, system, type, usability and skeptic on Lamps and Ladders and on Go, interaction on Go.
2. Drop the ladders and write each leg's length over its arc; Go's T1-11. Asked by system, style, interaction, usability and skeptic; the ladders are also retired in the tour lessons.
3. Close Status's 250px gap: a 15rem meter set beside the readout in the head row. Asked by feedback, soul, style, system, interaction and skeptic.
4. Title 'What's the plan?'. Asked by feedback, soul, system, interaction, type and skeptic.
5. Say each count once: the rail's Late against the head's '2 late', Setup against '3 to go', Ideas against '12 ideas'. Asked by skeptic, usability, system and feedback.
6. Status as ruled registers with the state in words in annunciator windows (Go's T1-13, from t1-b/variants/t1-console-refine status.html and sheet.css .annun). Asked by feedback (ruled rows), system (WORKING/OFF from Go), type (one register) and interaction.
7. The phosphor:
   - Aglow's curved glass: feedback, soul and system (t1-b/variants/t1-console-mut/sheet.css 1404-1430).
   - A tall, filled Next up tube: soul, style, feedback and skeptic on Go.
   - A deeper E7 pool: soul, and skeptic on Go.
   - Lit readout windows only for Today and Late: soul and style, within system's 'not every figure'.
8. Rail after the box in Tab order, and on the phone the box first: interaction and usability on Go; the tour lessons.
9. To do:
   - Drop the lamp column: system, usability.
   - A visible green 'Add something to do': interaction.
   - Go's amber late edge (T1-16).
   - Two-line due dates: type on Go (T1-14).
   - Edit keys and Show keys: interaction on Go.
10. Chat:
   - The wire down the whole thread with a stop at each speaker and a ring at the box: feedback.
   - Sentence-case bold names with mono times: type on Go.
11. The Plans track starts at Now, with no axis break: feedback, style, usability and skeptic.
12. Setup:
   - No hazard ladder: skeptic, usability.
   - Light the first unfinished step: interaction and feedback on Go.
   - Run-in bold actions: type on Go, as Lit Manual T1-05 sets them.
13. The rail the full width of its bay (system, feedback), with figures that do not float (type on Go).
14. The AVG pointer only when clear of the resting needle (style), and no bloom at 17px (soul).
15. Dotted card tops removed: style.
16. The flight-plan legs from lilac to a low-chroma steel-cyan: feedback.
17. The crew board's code made readable. Feedback asked for a legend; usability asked to drop the code. The marks now carry the rows' numbers and the words say the state.
18. One more grounded companion: system on Go (kind swatches kept, clay for restaurants). The tour lessons: amber leaking into kinds.
19. The kids' wishes get a count in their head row: interaction on Go.

briefs.name: Master Caution
briefs.title: What are we *planning*? This title is untried. It keeps the household 'we' that the 'What's next for us?' titles were liked for, without 'next', which narrowed the job and doubled the NEXT UP legend. The lit word 'planning' is the job itself. The ongoing tense covers what is being planned, kept for someday or needing a reminder, so ideas and wishes are not left out, and it reads as an invitation to tell Vera. It widens the search beyond the two settled phrasings. At 21 characters it is set clamp(1.75rem, 7.4vw, 2.25rem) with text-wrap: balance, so it holds one line at 390px and stays Home's largest head. It sits inside the box's frame as the textarea's <label>, with only 'planning' in .glow's two-layer halo.
briefs.hypothesis:
Lamps and Ladders' lower lenses fell on length and codes, not on its instruments. Three gems from designs that finished in the lower half, each rebuilt in the console's own terms, replace the console's weakest parts instead of adding beside them:
- Setup's hazard-striped ladder bay becomes one master caution line, the console's single amber light for 'something waits on an admin', as the same component on Home, Status and Settings.
- The Plans month's dead past folds away, and the flight plan is drawn into the weeks still to fly, so the figure and the grid become one drawing (the tour's 'a figure touches its rows').
- Every tube switches on with a roll bar.
A lit bus on Status's Who answers (from Evening Listing, Traced) carries light below the fold.

With the lineage's standing fixes applied, this keeps the graft's 8-plus in feedback, soul and style, and removes what cost it with interaction, usability and skeptic. Home is about 200px shorter, Plans shows the future at full height, and the light comes back in motion and on data.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-console-graft's files. Its structure stays recognisable at a glance: the readout rail, Next up's radar tube, the flight plan over Coming up, the crew board, the moving-coil meter, the jewelled lamps. The flight plan stays in the lineage's violet (#a191bd lines, #6d6280 flown), so the judges can compare it with the refinement's steel-cyan. Grafted features, each rebuilt in slate, steel, violet and phosphor: 1. MASTER CAUTION LINE: L042 (GEM) with L270. - Sources: Single Quote, r12-wild-4. Files: rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-4/sheet.css 'The strip along the screen when something waits on an admin' (about lines 1118-1137: .alert, .alert .legend, .alert-figure, .alert-one, .alert .rest) and its templates/home.html. Refined by Quote Board, r13-mut-3: rounds/r13/variants/r13-mut-3/templates/home.html lines 126-140, sheet.css .alert-figure and .alert-one at lines 1183-1185. - Build one component, section.caution, in sheet.css and a caution() macro in _ui.html. It is a 64px band the full width of the content, a slate (#111716) body under the bay's 2px top rule, with a 3px amber left edge. - In the band, in order: - a 44px sunk square window (#0b100e, inset 0 1px 3px #000a) holding the amber bar lamp lit from behind: the existing lamp('amber'), its glow tight at a -3px spread; - the legend in sentence case, Plex Sans Condensed 600 at 1.125rem, in ink; - the figure, e.g. '3 steps', in Plex Mono 600 amber; - the next thing as a link with a run-in bold action; - where there is more, the rest as short underlined links after 'then', in 14px ink-2; - a way on at the right. - Amber appears only in the lamp, the edge and the figure: never a fill, never a gradient. The band wraps to three lines on a phone, and every link keeps 44px. - HOME: it replaces section.bay.slim.setup (home.html, about lines 84-105, with its hold-gutter ladder), and the rail loses its Setup cell. It reads: 'Finish setting up · 3 steps · Choose your own password, so everybody signs in as themselves. · then Telegram, then Google Calendar · All the setup steps →'. It sits directly under the welcome console. With no setup left, nothing shows. - STATUS: under the head, while any row needs a look, the same line reads 'Needs a look · 1 · This page still uses the password the installer made up. · Choose your own →'. The rail drops its 'Needs a look' cell and keeps Working 5 · Off 7. - SETTINGS: 'Needs a look · 1 · Sign-in and security: still the password the installer made up. · Open it →'. The rail keeps Parts 9 · On 5. 2. FLOWN WEEKS FOLD, AND THE FLIGHT PLAN DRAWN INTO THE WEEKS TO FLY: L125 (GEM). - Source: Single Quote, r12-wild-4. Files: rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-4/sheet.css 'Days gone by step back into the dark' (about lines 1442-1452: table.month td.past, tr:has(> td.past:last-child) td { height: 2.75rem }, the inline .event) and its templates/plans_month.html. The same folding idea for quiet runs is L122 (Pocket Timeline, r11-wild-1). - On Plans > Month, a week wholly before today folds to a 2.75rem 'flown' strip: - day numerals in pewter Plex Mono 13px; - its plans as one-line chips led by the pewter flown ring (span.ring.past, plans_month.html line 10), with no time; - each chip a 44px hit area, which is the strip's own height. - Today's week and the weeks after keep full height (7rem minimum). - Remove the separate .month-fig strip above the table; it was 80% past. - Instead, before each unfolded week, add a 30px tr.legs row: a td colspan=7 holding an SVG whose x is (weekday + 0.5) / 7 × 100%. It draws that week's stretch of the flight plan: - the Now needle lit in today's column; - the live leg lit from Now to Next's jewel; - violet arcs between the later stops, each labelled with its length ('3 days') in Plex Mono 12px ink-2; - on each plan day, a numbered ring matching the ring on that day's chip. A leg that crosses the week's edge runs to the edge and resumes in the next week's leg row. - When the month shown does not contain today: no fold, no Now, violet legs only. - Without :has(), past weeks are only darker. - Weekend columns are shaded, and today's numeral sits in the steel key. - Rail: Today (lit clock) · Next up 'Silver Falls hike, tomorrow' · 'Still to come 2', counting what the unfolded week shows. 3. POWER-ON ROLL BAR ON EVERY TUBE: L110 (GEM). - Source: Attract Mode, r9-rand-1. File: rounds/r9/palettes/r9-rand-1.json, key 'css', the block '/* The monitors: a line of light passes down the glass as each switches on. */' (.crt::before and @keyframes scan). - Placement: Lamps and Ladders uses .crt::after for the power light, and .crt-tube::before / ::after for scanlines and falloff. So add an empty as the crt() macro's last child in the tube and draw the bar on it. - The bar is 2px: a white-hot core (color-mix(in srgb, var(--phosphor) 60%, #fff)) fading to phosphor at its ends, a 14px bloom, and an 18px wash trailing above it. - It runs once, top to bottom of the glass, over 1.2s, starting .1s after load, so the motion-on frames at 220ms and 450ms catch it mid-glass. Opacity goes 0.05 to 1 by 8%, holds .7 at 80%, then 0. - In the same beat the tube's content opens from a line: E16, already in the sheet, starting from opacity .05. - It runs on Next up, the Ideas radar, the Status meter, sign-in and the 404. Never on hover, never looping. Under reduced motion and more contrast: none. 4. THE LIT BUS ON WHO ANSWERS: L259, from Evening Listing, Traced (r12-idea-1). - File: rounds/r12/variants/r12-idea-1/palette.css 'Status: who answers is a chain' (about lines 714-723: .chain > .row::before, .row.on + .row.on > .x::before, .row.on:has(+ .row.on) > .x::after). - On Status's Who answers register only, a 1px pewter wire runs down through the rows' lamps. - Between two consecutive rows that are both on, it lights as a 2px phosphor bus with a 6px glow (chat to digest to lookups). Into the fallback's pewter ring it stays pewter and dashed: where answering would stop. - Keys and Connected to are plain registers, not chains. The words still say every state. THE LINEAGE'S STANDING FIXES, applied too: - Figures: - No zero-padding anywhere (remove every '%02d'); tabular figures. - Drop every ladder: the ladder() and nearness() macros, the hops, the chin, the setup gutter. - Over each Coming up arc, write its leg length; take the arithmetic from t1-b/variants/t1-console-refine/templates/home.html lines 16-30 and 113-180, and sheet.css .fig .track .leg at line 719. - The rail and counts: - The rail moves to after the box: it becomes the welcome console's foot strip, so the textarea is the first Tab stop after the nav. - Its cells are Go's: equal and full width, label over figure. - Only the Today clock is lit, green, in a small glass window. Late is amber ink with its bar lamp. - Say each count once: bay heads drop what the rail says ('2 late', '12 ideas'). - Status: - The meter is cut to 15rem and set in the head row beside the title and rail. - The AVG pointer is drawn only when 8 degrees or more from rest; no blooming 'AVG'. - The three banks become ruled registers side by side: a lamp, then the state word in a sunk window ('Working' / 'Off' / 'Needs a look', Plex Mono 600 13px), then the name and detail. No boxed cells. - To do: - A visible lit 'Add something to do' in the head row (Go's tasks.html
summary). - Delete the span.slot lamp column. - Late rows get a 3px amber edge and amber words, with two-line due dates (sans words over the mono date) and a 44px Edit key. - The crew board is words only: 'Alex · 1 late, 1 open', with no lamps and no legend. This is usability's ask, set against the refinement's numbered marks. - Chat: - The steel wire hangs from her glyph tile down the whole thread, with a stop per message (hers sage, her newest a lit jewel; the family's a steel ring with their initial). - A 1px pewter tick runs to each right-hand family bubble. - The wire ends in a lit ring at the box while it is the family's turn. - Names are sentence-case bold with mono times. - The tubes: - Aglow's curved glass: t1-b/variants/t1-console-mut/sheet.css 1404-1430. - The radar at full persistence. - Next up portrait, top-aligned and filled. - Home's E7 pool at full strength (about (37,80,52) under Send). - Cards: remove the punched dotted tops on Lately added and the Ideas cards. - Colour: the restaurant swatch in clay (people #bf8a6a); amber keeps one job. - 'Here' in the bar is a latched dark key: surface-3, a 2px steel cap (#a9c4d8) and the jewel lamp, in place of the full steel slab, which the tour's lessons retired as 'reads disabled' (T1-32). PAGES, in order: - HOME: - The welcome console: the tube on the left; on the right the speaker, then the box with the title in its frame, then the ways to start (three 44px sentence-case keys, 8px gap). The rail runs across the console's foot. - Then the master caution line, Coming up (violet flight plan with leg lengths and numbered rows), and the desk (To do with the words-only crew board; Lately added; the kids' wishes with a count). - Target 1500px or less. - PHONE: the box first, one-line title, ways to start, Next up, the rail in a 3×2 grid, the caution line, then the rest. - CHAT: as the fixes above. - IDEAS: the rail; the curved-glass radar with the roll bar; Nearest and Furthest set nowrap. - PLANS: the fold and the week legs. - TO DO: as the fixes above. - STATUS: head row with the meter, the caution line, the registers with the lit bus. - SETTINGS: the caution line, cards with lamps and state words. - FORM: one console bay, sunk fields lit while typed in, 'Add it' the one lit primary. Keep the kit's reduced-motion, more-contrast and forced-colours blocks. Nothing under 44px.

The lineage's fixes it also applies, with the lenses that asked:
- Zero-padding dropped: all eight lenses.
- Ladders out, and leg lengths from Go (T1-11): system, style, interaction, usability, skeptic.
- Rail after the box: interaction, usability.
- Counts said once: skeptic, usability, system.
- Meter at 15rem in the head row: feedback, soul, style, system, interaction, skeptic.
- Ruled registers with state words (T1-13): feedback, system, type, interaction.
- To do: Add primary (interaction), lamp column out (system, usability), amber edge and two-line dates (Go's T1-16 and T1-14).
- Crew board in words: usability.
- Chat wire the length of the thread: feedback. Sentence-case names: type.
- Curved glass (Aglow's T1-19): feedback, soul, system. Tall Next up: soul, style. Deeper pool: soul, skeptic.
- AVG pointer and its bloom: style, soul.
- Dotted card tops: style.

briefs.avoids:
- Setup's amber ladder read as hazard striping (skeptic) and as an unlabelled code (usability). The rail's 'Setup 03' beside '3 to go' said the count twice. The setup bay also made Home long; together these cost about 200px. One caution line answers all of it, and reuses the same component wherever something needs an admin, so amber keeps one job on every page.
- The Plans month track was 80% empty past (feedback, style, usability, skeptic), and the tour noted that Plans stayed an empty grid in every lineage but Pocket. The fold gives the height to the weeks to come, and the flight plan now touches its rows.
- Soul's 'the readout rail is matte' and the owner's 'bring back the phosphor effect': the roll bar and the lit bus put light on real events and data below the fold, not a lit window on every figure (system's and skeptic's warning).
- Status's 250px gap, boxed cells and the repeated 'Needs a look'.
- To do's second left-edge mark and missing Add primary.
- Tab order and counts said twice.
- The weak 'next' title.
- The one-sided chat wire, and tracked-caps call signs.
- The retired steel slab for 'here'.

It imports no main-line structure: no cased terminal column, no listing bands with a head column, no cut plate, no big quote. It also avoids the heat's converging devices: it has no NOW line across the To do list, the device Lit Manual owns in this heat.
